newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht eases slightly late, interbank lower.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht eases slightly late, interbank lower.

text.p: The Thai baht retreated slightly late on Thursday but the market remained cheered by the government's apparent willingness to involve the IMF in an economic rescue package, dealers said.
The Thai baht was quoted at 31.50-31.80 per dollar late onshore against 31.50-31.70 during the morning when it briefly spiked to 31.20.
Liquidity also eased as capital flowed into the market driving the overnight interbank offered rate down to 10-15 percent late against 15-17 percent this morning, dealers said.
Liquidity was also helped by the foreign banks onshore which were also offering at cheaper rates, dealers said.
"Liquidity is flush, the foreign banks onshore have been lending more cheaply," said one dealer at a foreign bank in Bangkok.
Spot trade in baht was active with the market taking encouragement from the IMF news though the baht's lustre faded slightly in the afternoon and trade remained volatile, dealers said.
"The IMF had more affect in the morning and the market is volatile and interest in both (dollar and baht)," he said.
"Right now the quote is quite stable. In the next few days I see the top quote capped at 32.00 and the bottom at 30.50," he added.
One month baht/dollar swap premiums were steady at 10/15 satang.
